meta.name: Neon Blackout
meta.description: A cyberpunk/synthwave design system on a near-black void. Neon is the only light source. Thirteen heritage colours from the Intersex-Inclusive Progress Pride flag, plus two signature neons that are ours.
meta.author: Anna
meta.authority: Rank 3 of 4. Authoritative for hex values, semantics, component specs and usage rules. README.md and CONTEXT.md outrank this file; neon-blackout.css and preview.html derive from it. See CONTEXT.md.

surfaces.description: Three surfaces. One is heritage: --remembrance-black's hex is the flag's Black stripe, so it carries the heritage name rather than a role name. Colour is emitted, never applied — surfaces exist to be punctuated by light.

void.name: Void
void.usage: Primary background. The dark everything sits in.

remembrance-black.name: Remembrance
remembrance-black.usage: Raised surface, disabled input background, skeleton base. Heritage.

text.description: Foreground lavender carries the words. Body text is never a neon hue.

heritage.description: The 13 colours of the Intersex-Inclusive Progress Pride flag, at the flag's own hex values. Heritage membership is a test, not a preference: a colour is heritage if it appears on the flag. These are never tuned — a heritage colour altered is a colour that no longer refers to the thing it is named for. Six ship without a UI role; being on the flag is reason enough.

swatches.note: Large text only. Below 4.5:1 on void.

signature.description: Ours, not flag colours. No magenta exists in the Progress Pride flag, and the flag's Trans Blue is #5ad4ec, not this turquoise. They carry flag-style names but are invented, and naming them as heritage would misrepresent the flag. Because they are ours, we revise them freely.

swatches.usage: Brand identity, primary action, key highlights
Focus rings, cursor, active element, ghost buttons, links

secondary.description: None. On the void, softer means mixing toward the void, and the tints below already do that at 12-15%. A system built on light surfaces has to invent this tier; here it already exists, built in the opposite direction.

tints.description: Accent background tints, computed rather than authored. Each is a color-mix of its token toward transparency over the void. Red sits higher because its tag places white text on it.

ansi.description: Standard ANSI c0-c15 terminal palette. Ships in this order for terminal themes. Consumed by hermes/skins/neon-blackout.yaml.

semantics.description: Colour-to-meaning mapping. Every role has exactly one colour, and no colour carries two roles. 'destructive' was an alias of 'error' at the same hex with a single consumer, and has been collapsed into it.

primary.usage: Brand, primary action buttons, key highlights

focus.usage: Focus rings, cursor, active element, ghost buttons, links

error.usage: Errors, destructive actions, alerts, danger buttons

success.usage: Success states, confirmed status, passing tests

accent.usage: Decorative accent. Large text only — 3.40:1 on void.

typography.description: Three-role type system, all SIL Open Font License, all self-hosted under fonts/. The stylesheet is the deliverable: dropping neon-blackout.css plus fonts/ into a project gets the real identity rather than a system fallback.

scale.description: 1.25 modular scale on a 16px base. --text-4xl is the ceiling: above it a heading is shouting rather than designing.

--text-xs.usage: Labels and badges. Body face only — mono does not use this step.

--text-sm.usage: Captions, meta, and all mono UI text

mono-floor.reason: Space Mono carries a small x-height for its size, and the densest text in this system is mono. The previous rule said 0.8rem and every mono component sat below it, which is what a minimum written as advice rather than expressed as a token looks like.

spacing.description: 8px-base spacing scale. All padding, margin, gap and dimensional values come from here. No arbitrary rem values.

--space-8.usage: Button Y, tag X, small gaps, list item Y

--space-12.usage: Button X, input X, list item X

--space-32.usage: Panel body roomy, section spacing top

border-radius.description: Four radii. --radius-md is the default for interactive elements.

glow.description: How this system renders neon: emission in darkness. Colours derive from palette tokens via color-mix and are never written as literals — a hardcoded rgba is a second source of colour that drifts silently.
glow.composition: Apply .glow (or .glow-text) plus one colour class plus one strength class. Add .glow-hover for interactive elements.
glow.uniform: Strengths are identical across all eight colours despite a five-fold luminance spread (violet 3.40:1 to yellow 16.85:1 against void). A per-colour ceiling was designed and rejected: perceived intensity is almost entirely the core, so capping the bloom is invisible, and capping the core removes the punch the system is built on.

controls.--glow-enabled: Set to 0 on :root or any subtree to disable the system outright.
controls.prefers-contrast-less: Lowers core alpha and every strength. This is where intensity is actually controlled — by what the viewer has already asked for.
controls.composition: Use glow-max on at most one element per view. A page where everything is at maximum has no hierarchy left, and accumulated bloom is where visual discomfort starts.

components.description: Every component the stylesheet ships, under the class names the stylesheet uses. Neither list may contain an entry the other lacks; tools/check-coherence.mjs verifies both directions.

utilities..glow: Box-shadow emission, pairs with a colour and a strength class

rules.description: How this palette behaves on the void.
do: Keep backgrounds in the void range and let foreground text breathe.
Pick one lead hue per surface as the dominant accent.
Map colour to meaning consistently across every screen.
Lean on glow for emphasis, not as a baseline texture.
Derive new accent backgrounds with color-mix from an existing token.
dont: Put two saturated hues at equal weight competing for the eye.
Use green as a general accent; it reads as success and nothing else.
Glow every element. The effect dies when it is everywhere.
Place body text in a neon hue. Foreground lavender carries the words.
Alter a heritage hex. It stops referring to the thing it is named for.
Write a colour literal where a token exists.

disabled.note: Buttons also get filter: grayscale(0.6). Inputs get background: var(--remembrance-black) and border-color: var(--line-soft).

loading.spinner: .spinner, or .btn.is-loading for an inline button spinner
loading.note: Loading buttons set color: transparent and pointer-events: none.

empty.note: Icon at 0.4 opacity, title in mono uppercase muted, description in body at --text-sm.
